verdict.rationale: LangGraph's interrupt() mechanism explicitly pauses graph execution at a node awaiting external input, and execution resumes via Command carrying the human's decision, backed by checkpointer-based state persistence for human-in-the-loop workflows; independent community commentary corroborates that its state-machine/time-travel design supports letting a human fix or redirect execution mid-run. Missing for 10: no independent hands-on reproduction of the exact pause/resume-with-decision flow beyond docs and general community praise.
